howto_md:
## How to use this booklet

This booklet is a map of the world's musical instruments. Every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what the instrument is, how it sounds, where it comes from and who made it famous. Every entry has an ID (such as INS-07.1) that is also its address on the website.

- **Parts** are the big branches (classification, families, world map, history, people, competitions, craft...).
- **Sections (INS-01, INS-02...)** are the main topics; each opens with a *Before you start* box.
- **Sub-sections and entries** carry a ☐ box: tick it when you have heard, seen or played the instrument.
- **Every instrument carries two labels**: the Indian class (Tata, Sushira, Avanaddha, Ghana) and the Hornbostel–Sachs class.
- **Registers** list 30 landmark instruments, the year-wise timeline and recent competition winners.
- **Tags** (#tata #sitar #rajasthan) and **See also** links connect related pages; genres and ragas link to the Music index (MUS).
- Start with **Part 0**, seven two-minute questions about how instruments sing.
howto_intro: This booklet is a map of the world's musical instruments: the two great classification systems, every family and type, India state by state, every continent, history, players and makers, competitions, the physics and craft of making, ideas and a buyer's guide. Every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what the instrument is and why it matters.
Every entry has an ID (such as INS-07.1 for Indian plucked lutes). The same ID is the entry's address on curioussparoows.com, where each one is growing into its own page.
howto_boxes: **Parts:** the intro questions, classification, families, the world map, history, people, competitions, craft, ideas, reviews, the practical guide, navigation and sources.
**Sections (INS-01 to INS-35):** the main topics, each opening with a *Before you start* box.
**Two labels on every instrument:** the Natyashastra class (Tata, Sushira, Avanaddha, Ghana) and the Hornbostel–Sachs class (idiophone, membranophone, chordophone, aerophone, electrophone).
**Registers:** 30 landmark instruments, the timeline and recent competition winners. They are a sourced selection; the full lists grow on the website.
**Step 2.** Learn the two classification systems in Part 1.
**Step 3.** Find your own state in Part 3, then travel to another continent.
**Step 4.** Follow tags and See also links; every genre and raga links to the Music index.
**Step 5.** Tick ☐ as you hear, see or play, and use the tracker at the end.

Knowledge belongs to the people who created it, players and makers alike. Every fact here stands on a source listed in Part 12, and every "latest" fact says when it was checked. Where something could not be verified, we say so instead of guessing. Found a mistake? Tell us, and we will fix it and thank you.
